facts.statement: Sibirotitan is a genus of somphospondyl sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Russia.
facts.quote: Sibirotitan ("Siberian titan") is a genus of somphospondyl sauropod from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian age) Ilek Formation of Russia.

facts.statement: The only known species of Sibirotitan is Sibirotitan astrosacralis.
facts.quote: The type and only species is S. astrosacralis.

facts.statement: Fossils of Sibirotitan were found at the Shestakovo 1 locality in the Ilek Formation near Shestakovo Village in West Siberia, Russia.
facts.quote: The material assigned to Sibirotitan was found in the Shestakovo 1 locality of the Ilek Formation, deposited in a cliff on the Kiya River's right bank, near Shestakovo Village in Kemerovo Province, West Siberia, Russia.

facts.statement: The genus Sibirotitan was formally named by Averianov and colleagues in 2018.
facts.quote: In 2018, Averianov et al. would name those which could be confidently referred to as the same taxon as S. astrosacralis

facts.statement: The genus name Sibirotitan combines the location Siberia with the Greek word for 'titan'.
facts.quote: The final name of Sibirotitan was derived from Siberia, where it was found, and the Greek Τιτάν (titan), the second group of divine beings in Greek Mythology, preceding the Olympians.

facts.statement: The species name astrosacralis refers to the star-like pattern of the sacral ribs seen from above.
facts.quote: The specific name S. astrosacralis is derived from the Greek ἄστρον, meaning "star", and Latin os sacrum, meaning "sacred bone". This refers to the star-like way in which the sacral ribs radiate in dorsal view.

facts.statement: Sibirotitan is considered one of the oldest known titanosauriform species found in Asia.
facts.quote: The authors noted that Sibirotitan was one of the oldest titanosauriform species discovered in Asia.

facts.statement: Sibirotitan lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 113 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período cretácico, entre 125 a 113 millones de años, durante el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: A particularly high hyposphene ridge on its dorsal vertebrae is the only unique distinguishing feature of Sibirotitan.
facts.quote: The hyposphene ridge on its dorsal vertebrae was particularly high, unlike other members of Titanosauriformes; this is the only autapomorphy of the taxon.

facts.statement: Sibirotitan is distinguished from other somphospondyls by having only five sacral vertebrae instead of the usual six.
facts.quote: Its possession of only five sacral vertebrae distinguishes it from all other somphospondyls, as possession of six is a synapomorphy of the clade.

facts.statement: Sibirotitan is estimated to have weighed around 20 tonnes, a size comparable to the Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: They found it roughly corresponded in size to that of the diplodocoid sauropod Apatosaurus, and suggested a similar size of 20 tonnes might have been possible.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis classifies Sibirotitan as a relatively advanced non-titanosaurian somphospondyl.
facts.quote: In this analysis, it was found to be a relatively advanced non-titanosaurian somphosondyl.

facts.statement: Sibirotitan is classified within the unranked family Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: It is proposed that later Asian sauropods may have given rise to the Lithostrotia group, though this remains a hypothesis.
facts.quote: it is proposed that one of these later taxa could have given rise to the Lithostrotia, a titanosaur group whose earliest representatives are Asian genera such as Tengrisaurus (from the Barremian or Aptian of Russia) and Jiangshanosaurus (from the Albian of China).

facts.statement: Definitive sauropod remains were discovered during expeditions in 1994 and 1995.
facts.quote: Los restos definitivos de saurópodos fueron descubiertos durante las expediciones hechas en 1994 y 1995.

facts.statement: In 2017, Averianov et al. named the specimens that could be referred safely to a single taxon S. astrosacralis.
facts.quote: en 2017 Averianov et al. les dieron nombre a los que podían ser referidos con seguridad a un mismo taxón, al que se le llamó S. astrosacralis.

facts.statement: This made it the second species named in the country after Tengrisaurus, named earlier in the same year.
facts.quote: Esto lo convierte en la segunda especie nombrada del país, tras Tengrisaurus, nombrado algo antes en el mismo año.

facts.statement: The species name S. astrosacralis is derived from the Greek word for "star" and the Latin word for "sacral bone".
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, S. astrosacralis se deriva del griego ἄστρον, astros, que significa "estrella", y el latín os sacrum, que significa "hueso del sacro".

facts.statement: The name refers to the star-like shape adopted by the sacral ribs when viewed from above.
facts.quote: Esto se refiere a la forma de estrella que adoptan las costillas del sacro al radiarse en vista dorsal.

facts.statement: The specimen PM TGU 120/10-Sh1-22, a dorsal vertebra, was selected as the holotype.
facts.quote: Entre sus fósiles, el espécimen PM TGU 120/10-Sh1-22, una vértebra dorsal, fue seleccionada como el holotipo.

facts.statement: The animal lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was found to share features of its vertebrae and ribs with Epachthosaurus and Euhelopus.
facts.quote: Se halló que compartía rasgos de sus vértebras y costillas con Epachthosaurus y Euhelopus.

facts.statement: In this analysis, it was determined to be a non-advanced titanosaurian somphospondyl.
facts.quote: En este análisis, se determinó que era un sonfospóndilo no titanosauriano avanzado.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Somphospondyli.
facts.quote: Parent group: Somphospondyli

facts.statement: It belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Researchers noted that teeth from the locality suggested a possible identity as a brachiosaurid, while a caudal vertebra from a nearby locality suggested the presence of a titanosaurian.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la localidad indicarían una posible identidad como un braquiosáurido, pero una vértebra caudal de una localidad cercana sugería igualmente la presencia de un titanosauriano.

facts.statement: Many referred specimens, though disarticulated, are believed to belong to a single individual, suggesting that large remains found in the 1960s may have been from the same skeleton as those found as recently as 2011.
facts.quote: Muchos de los especímenes referidos, aunque desarticulados, se cree que pertenecen a un único individuo; esto sugiere que los grandes restos hallados durante la década de 1960 pudieron haber sido del mismo esqueleto que los restos hallados después, tan recientemente como 2011.

facts.statement: A single centrum of a cervical vertebra was reported as belonging to a different juvenile individual, while the rest belongs to an adult animal.
facts.quote: Un único centro de una vértebra cervical fue reportado como perteneciente a un individuo juvenil diferente, mientras que el resto pertenece a un animal adulto.

facts.statement: Additionally, the authors noted that Sibirotitan was one of the oldest known sauropod species in Asia.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, los autores señalaron que Sibirotitan era una de las más antiguas especies de saurópodo conocidas de Asia.
